question: Which term is used for the tropical cyclone that originates in the north eastern Pacific and north Atlantic?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hurricane**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"Hurricane"** is used for tropical cyclones that form in the **North Atlantic** Ocean and the **Northeastern Pacific** Ocean (east of the International Date Line).
 
• Hurricanes **are characterized by strong winds, heavy rainfall, and can cause significant damage in coastal and inland areas**.
 
• Hurricane**s typically form in tropical regions where the sea surface temperature is at least 26.5°C (about 80°F**).
 
• This warmth provides the necessary heat and moisture to fuel the storm.
 
• A** hurricane has a well-defined center called the eye**, which is calm and clear, surrounded by a rotating mass of strong winds and rain, known as the **eyewall**.
 
• The storm extends for hundreds of miles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Typhoon**:

 
 
• A tropical cyclone like a hurricane but forms in the Northwest Pacific Ocean (west of the International Date Line).
 
 
 
• **Twister (Tornado)**:
 
 
• A small but extremely powerful rotating column of air, forming in severe thunderstorms. Tornadoes are highly localized and can have wind speeds exceeding 300 mph.
 
 
 
• **Tornado**:
 
 
• Another name for **twister**, this term refers to a localized and intense storm with rotating winds that can cause massive damage over a small area.
